findings.text: The task status formatter produces one decimal record for a single thread, starting with the namespaced process identifier followed by the command name in parentheses and a single state character, then a fixed sequence of numeric fields covering parent, group, session, terminal, flags, fault counts, CPU times, priority, thread count, start time, memory sizes, register snapshot, masked signal sets, wait-channel presence flag, processor, scheduling class and delay accounting, plus gated memory addresses and exit status, ending with newline and releasing acquired references.

Numeric address and data-range fields derived from the memory descriptor are only disclosed when the caller is permitted and a descriptor is present; otherwise the formatter emits placeholder values, with code boundaries using one and stack, data, argument and environment ranges plus exit code using zero.

Internal monotonic durations are rendered as clock ticks, priority values are scaled to the traditional Unix nice interval, start time is adjusted by a time-namespace boot-time offset before conversion, and legacy signal bitmaps are reduced to standard signals by retaining only low bits for compatibility.
Under paged memory management the virtual size helper reports total mapped pages scaled by page size.
Without paged translation the virtual size helper walks all mapped areas under a read lock and sums each area length to obtain the total span.
Two per-thread status entry points forward to a shared formatter with a flag distinguishing thread versus group presentation.

The resident-set summary entry reports seven decimal counters for size, resident, shared, text, placeholder, data and placeholder followed by newline, or all zeros when the target has no memory descriptor, releasing the descriptor after sampling.

With paging, shared pages combine file-backed and shared-memory counters, text size derives from aligned code boundaries shifted to pages, data combines anonymous data and stack usage, resident adds anonymous pages to shared, and the return value is total virtual pages.

Without paging, size accumulates per-object overheads plus region extents, text derives from aligned code boundaries, data derives from the stack-to-data span, the byte total is shifted to pages and augmented by text and data to form both the return value and resident count, while the shared output location is not written by the shown logic.

Child lookup resolves the parent from the inode, holds the global task list for reading throughout the search, prefers resuming from a previously returned child when it remains a direct child with siblings, otherwise scans the child list by position, and returns a referenced child identifier or null when absent or at end.

The children sequence iterator starts by position without a previous element, advances by requesting the next child after the current one while dropping the old reference and incrementing position, terminates by dropping the current reference, and displays each element as a namespaced decimal identifier followed by a space.
A read-only sequential file binds open, read, seek and release to the children iterator, with open attaching the iterator operations to the file.

Directory entries for per-process nodes carry a name pointer, precomputed length, mode with file type, optional inode and file operation pointers, and a discriminated operation union; helper constructors build directory, link, regular, single-display and attribute entries with appropriate types, permissions and callbacks.
Initial link count for a per-process directory starts at two and increments once per contained directory entry.

Root and current-directory link resolvers lock the target task, copy its filesystem root or working directory path when present, unlock, and report missing entry when no filesystem context exists, with the root variant delegating to a shared helper.

Command-line retrieval snapshots argument and environment boundaries under a spin lock, rejects empty or inverted ranges, allows title overwrites that extend into the environment area, detects overwritten titles by inspecting the final argument byte and then serves a single-page title prefix including its terminator, otherwise serves the argument range in page-sized remote reads with user copies, honoring file position and requested length.

The command-line file read resolves the target thread from the inode, returns a missing-process error when absent, delegates to the memory-based reader, advances the file position only on positive transfer, and releases the thread reference; its operation table exposes read and generic seek.

The wait-channel display acquires the execution-update lock in killable mode, emits zero when the caller lacks read permission, otherwise resolves the blocking address and prints its symbolic name when known, falling back to zero, always releasing the lock.

Tracing access first takes the execution-update lock for reading in killable mode, then verifies attach permission and releases the lock with a permission error on denial; the paired unlock releases the read hold.

Kernel stack disclosure through the stack file is limited to administrators, uses a fixed maximum depth, allocates a temporary buffer for addresses, captures the target stack only after successful trace locking, prints one address per line in symbolic backtrace form, and always frees the buffer.
Scheduler statistics emit three zeros when scheduler accounting is disabled, otherwise the accumulated execution time, total delay and scheduling count.

Latency display opens as a single-read sequence showing a version header followed by per-slot count, time, maximum and symbolic backtrace entries for non-empty slots, while writes clear the target tracing state and report full consumption; the file operations expose open, read, write, seek and release.

Out-of-memory score adds a base of one thousand to badness scaled per mille of total pages including swap, then takes two thirds, yielding zero when badness indicates the protected minimum, and prints the result with newline.

Resource-limit display pairs each limit index with a human-readable name and an optional unit string, covering processor, file, memory, process, locking, signal, queue and scheduling limits in table order.

Limits display snapshots all soft and hard values under the signal-handler lock, prints a fixed column header, then one row per limit showing names with decimal values or the word unlimited and trailing units when defined.

System-call display holds trace permission across sampling, reports running when no call is captured, shows number plus stack and instruction pointers for negative numbers, otherwise shows number, six arguments and both pointers.
Attribute changes that include mode bits are rejected as not permitted; other attributes proceed through prepare and copy helpers and report their status.
Non-paged memory-size helpers hold the memory-map read lock while iterating areas and release it before returning.
Task status and wait-channel readers hold the execution-update read lock across sampling and release it on all paths, with status also releasing the memory reference when taken.
Maximum captured kernel stack depth for the per-task stack file is 64 entries.
The memory-summary fallback line contains seven zeros, and each child identifier in the children file is followed by a space.
Memory-force override accepts three named levels always, ptrace and never with corresponding ordered enumerators.

Early boot parsing of the memory-force option preserves the configured default when the parameter is missing or unrecognized and otherwise stores the looked-up level, reporting invalid input only when no value is supplied.
Children enumeration is explicitly best-effort under concurrency and may skip entries when siblings exit between reads; precise results require the leader and children to be stopped or frozen.
The status formatter never emits raw kernel addresses, replacing the wait-channel address with a presence flag and gating code, stack and data addresses plus exit status behind a permission check.
